test_title: PYST 35: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 23th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true about the Deogarh temple built in the early 6th century CE?

options.text: It follows a panchayatana layout and is an early example of Nagara style.
It was built by Chandela rulers and faces east like most Hindu temples.
Its main deity is Shiva in the form of Mahadeo.
It is entirely rock-cut with vaulted interiors.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It follows a panchayatana layout and is an early example of Nagara style.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Deogarh temple**, also known as the Dashavatara Temple, was constructed in the **early 6th century CE**. It is one of the earliest surviving examples of Hindu temple architecture.

• The temple follows a **panchayatana layout**, a style where the main shrine is surrounded by four subsidiary shrines. This layout is a hallmark of early Hindu temple design.

• The architectural style of the temple is classified as **Nagara style**, which is characterized by its curvilinear shikhara (tower) and intricate carvings.

• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Vishnu**, as evidenced by the presence of sculptures depicting Vishnu's incarnations (Dashavatara).

• The temple's **ornamentation and sculptural reliefs** are considered masterpieces of ancient Indian art and provide insights into the religious themes and artistic conventions of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Deogarh Temple's Panchayatana Layout:**

• The term **panchayatana** refers to a layout where a central shrine is surrounded by four subsidiary shrines, symbolizing the presence of other deities alongside the main deity.

• This architectural design reflects the **syncretic nature** of Hinduism, accommodating multiple deities within a single sacred complex.

• **Nagara Style Architecture:**

• The **Nagara style** is predominantly found in northern India and is marked by its **beehive-shaped shikhara** (tower) rising over the sanctum sanctorum.

• The style emphasizes verticality and intricate carvings, often depicting mythological and religious motifs.

• The Deogarh temple is an **early example** of this style and showcases its formative features.

• **Historical Context:**

• The temple was likely constructed during the reign of the **Gupta Empire**, a period renowned for cultural and artistic achievements.

• The Gupta period is often referred to as the **"Golden Age of India"**, and the Deogarh temple reflects the sophisticated architectural and artistic norms of the era.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Option 2:** The temple was not built by the Chandela rulers, as they came much later (9th-13th century CE). Incorrect.

• **Option 3:** Its main deity is Vishnu, not Shiva as Mahadeo. Incorrect.

• **Option 4:** The temple is not entirely rock-cut; it is constructed using stone blocks. Incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Gupta Period Art and Architecture:**

• Known for its refinement and sophistication, the Gupta era marked significant advancements in temple construction, sculpture, and painting.

• Religious themes, particularly those associated with **Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism**, dominated artistic expressions.

• **Significance of the Deogarh Temple:**

• The temple provides valuable insights into the development of Hindu temple architecture and early iconography.

• It is a key resource for understanding the transition from **wooden structures to stone temples** in ancient India.
